text:
Maya: canary for axiom14b:quant-v2 showing slab fragmentation spikes and 2 OOMs during burst sim. p99 latency ~12% worse vs fp16. pasting canary config and quick notes.

Sam: paste config?

Maya: config snippet: batching batch_size=8 microbatch=2 max_inflight=4; defaults max_new_tokens=256 prefetch=true slab_reserve_kb=256

Oliver: looks like prefetch + microbatching -> slab churn. quick mitigations: reduce batch_size to 2, microbatch to 1, disable prefetch, set max_new_tokens=80, bump slab_reserve_kb=512, enable soft_eviction. watch KV cache for long sessions.

Jordan: any quality regressions on eval? quant kernels can change numerics for long summaries.

Maya: short eval run showed ~1.3% AUC drop on long-summary set, a few coherence failures. opened eval run eval/axiom14b/quant-v2/2026-03-21 and GH issue with diffs.

DeployBot: canary started on pool canary-2 at 2026-03-21T09:12:00Z

Maya: ran small experiment with reduced config: batch_size=1 microbatch=1 max_new_tokens=80 prefetch=false slab_reserve_kb=512 soft_eviction=true. 10k burst sim -> 0 OOMs, p99 improved ~15% vs prior canary, throughput down ~7%. fragmentation much lower.

Sam: propose router rule: if expected_tokens>200 or input_tokens>4096 -> route to axiom14b:fp16. add auto-fallback on OOM.

Oliver: agree. add policy: expected_tokens>200 => fp16 and alert/rollback if p99_degradation>8% for 15m.

Maya: action items: pause rollout, patch canary defaults (max_new_tokens=80 batch_size=2 prefetch=false), run per-layer qconfig sweep (try symmetric per-channel + tighter clipping), run 5k long-context evals, link GH issue #1428. cc @Sam @Oliver

Sam: i'll add router rule and rollback alert.

Jordan: add synthetic monitor comparing quant p99 to fp16 p99; page if quant_p99 > fp16_p99*1.08 for 15m.

Maya: will post eval results here when done. thanks.
